newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Feb 11.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Feb 11.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Tuesday morning:
** India's fiscal deficit target for 1997/98 (April-March) expected to be pegged between 4 and 4.5 percent of GDP, the Business Standard quotes government sources as saying
** Landslide victory for Sikh-Hindu alliance in elections to Punjab state legislature should reduce pressure on Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's United Front alliance, analysts say
They say the Congress is likely to scale down its frequent threats to topple the United Front alliance, which took power last June, and force mid-term elections at the national level

** Morgan Stanley group chairman Richard Fisher tells Economic Times in interview he is bullish on Indian capital markets. He admits his company has suffered a negative image among domestic investors because of the poor returns on Morgan's mutual fund floated at the end of 1993
** India raises price of retail sugar for sale through its public rationing system to 10.50 rupees per kg from 9.05 rupees in order to cut subsidies, a government spokesman says
** Japan's Mitsubishi Corp is discussing a clutch of high-profile investments topped by $2.0 billion telecommunications joint venture, a senior company official says
** India is inching towards approval of a landmark proposal from the Tata group to set up a domestic airline in partnership with Singapore Airlines, government official says
"It is likely to come through," the official, who is close to negotiations, said of the Tatas' $600-million plan which has divided India's ruling coalition
** Essar Oil has sold two off-shore rigs for 1.9 billion rupees, the Financial Express says. It says the company has decided to shift its focus from off-shore drilling to onshore drilling
** Six new steel projects which will together produce an additional 4.85 million tonnes of the metal are on the anvil, the Economic Times says
